correctness.rationale: The stationary Gaussian two-filter model is AR(2) with coefficients sum/product of its stable poles. Yule--Walker at lags one and two recovers the unordered poles algebraically, and the distinct environmental colors identify the sole common pole. Explicit exact variance and cross-covariance identities recover the innovation covariance, with positive denominators. Swapping equal site colors with the demographic pole preserves the entire bivariate Gaussian process. A local one-parameter deformation preserves all listed lag-zero/lag-one moments and strict covariance positive definiteness. Exact rational checker passed 30 tests including repeated roots, and finite checks are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Comparison with the full motivating Moran-effect article and accessible ecology/ARMA identification papers found forward correlation, observation-error estimation or general identification frameworks, but no explicit statement or established implication of the two-site colored-environment exact inverse, equal-color full-law obstruction and sharp listed-moment boundary. The classical Yule--Walker pole recovery is cited as prior mathematical machinery, not as a novel lemma. Residual risk from partially inaccessible general ARMA identification literature remains.
residual_risks: General multichannel ARMA and rational systems-identification theory may imply the pole-intersection criterion as a special case; accessible abstracts did not resolve that comparison.
Full proof text of Dennis (2006), Knape (2008) and older generic time-series identification articles was not available for conclusive exclusion.
No claim of exhaustive uniqueness in unpublished manuscripts is made.

value.rationale: Unmeasured colored environmental forcing confounds local density regulation in ecological population monitoring. The theorem supplies a complete, constructive sharp distinction: identical environmental colors permit global Gaussian observational equivalence, whereas two different site colors identify common demographic relaxation and innovation covariance from a small exact-moment collection. It gives a principled monitoring-design criterion, rather than an arbitrary parameter computation; estimation noise and model extensions are explicitly excluded.
